changes: Viewport-bounded rasters for unscrolled overflow-hidden subtrees of at most 64 DOM nodes
25 percent capacity headroom rounded to 64 CSS pixels; shrink only below half capacity
Immediate visible refill after capacity or scroll-mode changes, including with pending work
Ordinary wheel scrolling, any scripted scrolling, and dense subtrees retain full raster coverage
CPU limits, sandbox policy and animation semantics unchanged

component.method: Three serial ABBA/BAAB/ABBA runs; 12 warmup states and 60 measured states per mode, same release test bundle, process CPU across threads. Document construction/layout and installed pixel checks outside timing. This measures the scroll raster component, not end-to-end widget CPU or display FPS.

live.method: Serial published baseline, viewport-bounded scroll rasters and sandbox-backed WebKit; reverse order in round two. Same fixtures and CPU quotas. CPU is percent of one core including WebKit helpers, excluding WindowServer. Host callbacks are not display FPS. No direct-surface experiment included

single_run_controls.method: Serial published baseline, viewport-bounded scroll rasters and sandbox-backed WebKit; reverse order in round two. Same fixtures and CPU quotas. CPU is percent of one core including WebKit helpers, excluding WindowServer. Host callbacks are not display FPS. No direct-surface experiment included

validation.pixel_matrix_provenance: Selected pixel test rerun from the preserved final release test bundle with stdout/stderr separated after the full suite log interleaved one result; one test passed, zero failures

clipped_panels: Both renderers: built 48 panels using the corrected batched control, scrolled to panel 48 and back, no sandbox stop
Both renderers: deterministic freeze at 24 panels/frame 25, reveal distant content and return, matching visible geometry
Both renderers: resized window from 480 to 390 CSS pixels and checked wrapped controls and clipping
Native: 48-to-12 count change, pause, reset to epoch 3, resume control and freeze back to frame 25
WebKit: reset to epoch 1 and verified resumed progress from frame 25 to frame 47
clipped_ticker: Both renderers: pause/resume, width locking/unlocking, 480-to-390 CSS-pixel resize, scrolling through S120 and back
Native and WebKit displayed changing readings and track positions after resume, without blank clipped areas
limitations: The dense native case remains visibly slow and can show different tile generations during motion; static freeze settles correctly. No displayed-FPS claim is made.
The first 48-panel control implementation exceeded the JavaScript event quota; it was corrected to build four panels per timer before the successful manual pass.

The live benchmark used the earlier control implementation at its unchanged default 24-panel workload; the fixture hash records that source. The final control revision is separately checked in frozen-controls.
manual.cleanup: Both test apps closed after manual checks; no user app was stopped.

limitations: Host callbacks are not displayed frames or equal completed painting
The new dense fixture uses the unchanged full-raster path and remains much slower than sandbox-backed WebKit
Dense native throughput varies substantially when the existing sustained-render budget changes throttle state; its median differences are not attributed to the optimization
The single-run controls do not support precise speedup claims
The raster microbenchmark excludes document construction, layout, JavaScript and presentation

direct_iosurface.decision: Removed: small own-process gains did not establish a total benefit and WindowServer CPU rose.

fixed_work_control_attempt.decision: All states and pixel checks completed, but the contained control had 60 or 61 layouts across runs. The runner rejected equal-work attribution for that mode. This used the unrestricted headroom candidate, not the final guarded candidate.

report.method: Two prebuilt renderer XCTest bundles, 120 tracks and 60 completed mutation states per mode. Separate serial processes use identical optimization settings. One state in flight; document and scroll tile completion checked. Applied state and installed-tree pixel checks run outside measured intervals. Process CPU includes worker threads. Elapsed time includes completion barriers. Work equality requires identical completed state, layout, document job, document install, scroll raster, tile job and compositor raster counts across all rounds of each mode. Renderer callbacks are not treated as completed frames. This is a renderer-component comparison, not WebKit, full-host throughput or display FPS. The checkout workload source and both bundle executable hashes must remain unchanged throughout the comparison; callers must build both bundles from the same workload source.
report.order: Before then after in round 1; reversed in alternate rounds
